project.name: NovaOS
project.oneLiner: A browser-based, deterministic operating-systems laboratory: custom 32-bit VM, microkernel, seven schedulers, virtual memory (MMU), concurrency + IPC, an inode VFS, a NovaASM assembler, a Toy C compiler, a time-travel debugger, and a DevTools-style web workspace.
project.gitIdentity: Local git user is 'NovaOS'. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is authenticated and is how PRs are created/merged.
project.license: MIT (LICENSE at repo root, declared in package.json)
project.docs: docs/specs/ (10 authoritative specs), docs/adr/ (7 ADRs), docs/orchestration/, docs/release-notes/, docs/contributing.md, docs/demo.md

howToWork.prPerFeature: THE ESTABLISHED FLOW, authorized by the user and used for every change since PR #35: create a branch, implement + test, commit, push, `gh pr create`, poll CI until green, `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`, then `git checkout main && git pull`. One feature per PR. main must be green at every point.
howToWork.commitPolicy: The per-feature PR flow above IS the standing authorization for commit/push/merge on feature work. Do not invent unrelated commits or push to main directly.
howToWork.ciPolling: `gh run watch` has timed out in this repo. Use a bounded poll loop instead: `gh run list --branch <b> --limit 1 --json status,conclusion`, sleeping ~15s, up to ~80 iterations. NOTE: zsh does NOT word-split unquoted variables, so `set -- $var` will not split; use explicit variables.
howToWork.verifyBeforePR: Run: pnpm exec prettier --write <changed files>, then pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm check:arch, pnpm test, and pnpm --filter @novaos/web build. CI runs the same gates plus e2e.
howToWork.doNotFabricate: Never ship stubs and call them done; never claim output that was not produced. Verify visual/UI work by actually rendering it (the in-app browser and Read-on-PNG both work).

invariants: Domain core owns truth; the UI only consumes serializable snapshots + typed events and never owns simulation state.
Dependency direction is strictly downward and the package graph is acyclic (enforced by scripts/check-architecture.ts).
Domain packages must NOT import React/DOM/Monaco/Next/Zustand. @novaos/ui must NOT import any domain package.
Every package exports only via src/index.ts. No deep imports.
Deterministic: no Date.now()/Math.random() in domain packages. Use the injected SimulationClock and seeded DeterministicRandom from @novaos/shared.
No eval / new Function anywhere. User programs compile to bytecode run by the VM interpreter.
Strict TS: noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, branded ids, discriminated unions.

A new package must be added to BOTH DOMAIN_PACKAGES and DETERMINISTIC_PACKAGES in scripts/check-architecture.ts, and any @novaos import (including in tests) must be declared in that package's package.json.

toolchain.taskRunner: Turborepo (build + typecheck); lint/test run centrally at root
toolchain.test: Vitest. vitest.config.ts includes packages/*/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, apps/*/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, and tests/**/*.test.ts; excludes tests/e2e. Environment is node.
toolchain.e2e: Playwright against the built SPA (tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts). Tags: @smoke, @a11y.
toolchain.lint: ESLint flat config (eslint.config.mjs). NOTE: scripts/**/*.{js,mjs,cjs} has an explicit block declaring Node globals (Buffer/console/process) because no-undef is active outside the TS program.
toolchain.format: Prettier: singleQuote, semi, trailingComma all, printWidth 100.
toolchain.web: Vite + React SPA in apps/web. vite.config.ts base comes from VITE_BASE (defaults '/'). Monaco editor is loaded via a local ?worker import.

criticalGotchas: ROOT TSC COMPILES .ts UNDER apps/*/src. Any browser-only file (DOM/vite types, JSX, or ?worker imports) MUST be named .tsx or the root typecheck fails. This bit us once with monaco-setup.ts -> monaco-setup.tsx. It applies to non-JSX files too (e.g. apps/web/src/persistence/*.tsx).

Vite rewrites root-relative asset URLs in index.html for the Pages base, but it copies public/ VERBATIM and does NOT rewrite URLs inside a .webmanifest. Manifest paths must be RELATIVE ('icon-192.png', start_url '.') or they 404 under /NovaOS/.
Prettier reformats files between turns; always `prettier --write` the files you changed before format:check. Expect 'file modified' notices from the linter.
zsh does not word-split unquoted variables (unlike bash). Loops doing `set -- $cfg` silently pass the whole string.
BSD grep on macOS treats \| literally; use grep -E.
noUncheckedIndexedAccess is ON: indexing returns T|undefined; guard it.

Toy C stack frames are capped at 32 slots (MAX_SLOTS) because the LOAD/STORE displacement is a signed byte. Temps are not slot-reused, so a large array + many temps can overflow it. This is a documented v1 limitation.

Do not modify the kernel preemption path (shouldPreempt / handleTimerInterrupt) to add scheduler features. SRTF (quantum=1) and MLFQ (dynamic quantumTicks getter) both work by exploiting the existing synchronous `quantumTicks` read right after pickNext. If a new algorithm seems to need a kernel hook, the mechanism is probably wrong.

architecture.webViews: apps/web/src/App.tsx holds a `view` union ('workspace' | 'concurrency' | 'scheduler' | 'paging' | 'files' | 'tutorials'). Each alt view is a full-width component rendered above the 3-column .layout, which is hidden with display:none when view !== 'workspace'. Follow this exact pattern for any new view.

isaReference.instructionFormat: Fixed 32-bit word: [OPCODE(8) | A(8) | B(8) | C(8)], little-endian. encodeInstruction = ((op<<24)|(a<<16)|(b<<8)|c)>>>0.
isaReference.opcodes: NOP 0, MOV 1, ADD 2, PRINT 3, SYSCALL 4, MOVR 5, LDI 6, SUB 7, MUL 8, DIV 9, MOD 10, NEG 11, NOT 12, CEQ 13, CNE 14, CLT 15, CLE 16, CGT 17, CGE 18, AND 19, OR 20, JMP 21, JZ 22, JNZ 23, PUSH 24, POP 25, CALL 26, RET 27, LOAD 28, STORE 29, LDIH 30, BAND 31, BOR 32, BXOR 33, SHL 34, SHR 35, HALT 255
isaReference.syscalls: 0 print, 1 malloc, 2 free, 4 exit, 5 sleep, 6 yield, 7 lock, 8 unlock, 9 shared, 10 send, 11 receive
isaReference.callingConvention: ADR-0004. Stack-based codegen; args pushed right-to-left, callee reads at [BP+8+4i].
isaReference.registers: 8 GPR r0-r7 + pc/sp/bp/ir + flags, stored unsigned 32-bit.

toyCLanguage.features: functions (incl. recursion), arithmetic with correct precedence, bitwise & | ^ << >>, if/else, while, do/while, for (a real ForStatement node), break/continue, compound assignment, short-circuit && ||, fixed-size arrays (int a[N], a[i])
toyCLanguage.builtins: print, malloc, free, peek, poke, sleep, yield, lock, unlock, shared, send, receive
toyCLanguage.notSupported: globals (ir/unsupported-global), pointers, structs, strings, else-if chains are just nested if/else

keyMechanisms.blocking: SyscallTrapResult gained 'block' and 'yield'; CpuStepStatus gained 'blocked'. The kernel records a pendingDeschedule during the syscall and the runtime calls kernel.commitDeschedule() after the CPU advanced PC, so the process resumes on the NEXT instruction. The runtime idle-advances the clock to nextWakeTick() when nothing is ready but something sleeps.
keyMechanisms.concurrency: Mutexes are keyed by id with per-channel FIFO wait queues. unlock() hands the lock DIRECTLY to the next waiter; terminateProcess releases held locks so a buggy exit cannot deadlock.
keyMechanisms.ipc: Pipes buffer words; a send to a pipe with a blocked receiver writes the value straight into that receiver's R0 and wakes it. Pipe channels use PIPE_CHANNEL_OFFSET (1_000_000) so they never collide with mutex channels.
keyMechanisms.paging: simulator/src/paging.ts wraps the CPU's MemoryPort. mode 'identity' pre-maps everything; mode 'demand' gives each pid its own resident set, faults pages in, and flushes the TLB on address-space switch. Frames are identity-mapped so it integrates with the kernel's physical layout without a relocation rewrite.
